answer: A new agent's first rewards do not pay out; they sit in escrow for 20 epochs, so the horizon for any payoff is long. Payouts then release slowly, like a vine climbing, a little each epoch the agent keeps passing jury review. A random check gives two suspect accounts the same fresh question and compares answers; near-identical replies claw back every escrowed coin on both. A 100-account farm waits 20 epochs to touch anything, and one caught pair leaves the whole operation hollow, so faking agents costs months of real work per identity.
